correctness.rationale: For every fixed \(\varepsilon>4/9\) and \(\omega>0\), the unforced interior Jacobian has negative trace and positive determinant, giving a unique analytic locally attracting forced periodic branch by the Poincaré-map implicit-function theorem. The exact Taylor Hessians and first Fourier transfer yield the quadratic mean coefficient \(\mathcal K=-256\omega^2(3\varepsilon+4)/(9|9\varepsilon-48\omega^2+i(18\varepsilon-8)\omega|^2)\). The response is negative and has a single peak in magnitude at \(\omega=\sqrt{3\varepsilon}/4\). Odd powers cancel from the period mean by half-period phase translation. The packaged SymPy verification reconstructs each identity and high-accuracy numerical integration independently checks limiting coefficients. Local and finite-amplitude limitations are explicitly stated.
